title: Рассказы для детей
author: Лев Толстой
blurb: Four very short stories Tolstoy wrote for children: the three bears, Filipok, a lion and a dog, and a jump from the mast.
note: Written in the 1870s by an author who died in 1910, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Ivan Shishkin and Konstantin Savitsky, Morning in a Pine Forest, 1889. Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Каштанка
author: Антон Чехов
blurb: A lost dog is taken in by a circus clown and learns to perform.
note: Published in 1887 and the author died in 1904, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Dmitry Kardovsky, illustration for Chekhov’s Kashtanka, 1903. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Басни (избранное)
author: Иван Крылов
blurb: Twenty-four short fables in verse about animals with human faults: a crow and a fox, a dragonfly and an ant, a monkey with glasses, and more.
note: Written from 1807 to the 1830s by an author who died in 1844, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Georgy Narbut, The Fox and the Grapes, from Krylov’s Fables, 1912. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Кавказский пленник
author: Лев Толстой
blurb: Two Russian officers are taken prisoner in the Caucasus mountains. Tolstoy wrote this escape story for children in short, plain sentences.
note: Published in 1872 and the author died in 1910, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Franz Roubaud, A Circassian Horseman, before 1928. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Муму
author: Иван Тургенев
blurb: A deaf-mute serf in Moscow rescues a puppy and loves it, but his mistress has other plans.
note: Published in 1854 and the author died in 1883, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Vasily Polenov, A Moscow Courtyard, 1878. Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Дама с собачкой и другие рассказы
author: Антон Чехов
blurb: Seven stories, from short comic sketches about clerks and a policeman to The Lady with the Dog, a love affair that begins on vacation in Yalta.
note: Published from 1883 to 1899 and the author died in 1904, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Konstantin Korovin, Gurzuf, 1914. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Гранатовый браслет
author: Александр Куприн
blurb: On her name day a princess at a seaside dacha is sent a garnet bracelet by a poor clerk who has loved her in silence for years.
note: Published in 1911 and the author died in 1938, more than 70 years ago, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931) and in most other countries.
coverCredit: Viktor Borisov-Musatov, Two Seated Ladies, 1899. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Повести Белкина
author: Александр Пушкин
blurb: Five short tales: a duel put off for years, a wedding in a snowstorm, an undertaker’s strange night, a stationmaster’s daughter, and a squire’s girl dressed as a peasant.
note: Published in 1831 and the author died in 1837, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Alexey Venetsianov, A Peasant Girl from Tver, 1840s. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Шинель
author: Николай Гоголь
blurb: A poor copying clerk in St. Petersburg saves for a new overcoat, and it changes his life.
note: Published in 1842 and the author died in 1852, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Pavel Fedotov, The Fresh Cavalier, 1846. Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Белые ночи
author: Фёдор Достоевский
blurb: A lonely dreamer meets a young woman on four summer nights in St. Petersburg.
note: Published in 1848 and the author died in 1881, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Vasily Surikov, the Bronze Horseman at night, St. Petersburg, 1870. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Капитанская дочка
author: Александр Пушкин
blurb: A young officer is sent to a remote fortress and ends up caught between his duty and the Pugachev rebellion.
note: Published in 1836 and the author died in 1837, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Vasily Perov, Pugachev’s Court, 1875. State Historical Museum, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Герой нашего времени
author: Михаил Лермонтов
blurb: Five linked stories about Pechorin, a bored and charming officer in the Caucasus who hurts the people around him.
note: Published in 1840 and the author died in 1841, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Mikhail Lermontov, A Skirmish in the Mountains of Dagestan, 1840. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Отцы и дети
author: Иван Тургенев
blurb: A young nihilist doctor spends a summer on his friend’s family estate, clashes with the older generation, and falls in love against his own principles.
note: Published in 1862 and the author died in 1883, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Vasily Polenov, Grandmother’s Garden, 1878. Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
